agent.result_text:
The floor now comes before the late charge, but `bin/e2e` is not fully green: 2 of the 4 tests pass. The other two fail on things outside this change that I left alone.

**What changed**
- **Server** (`statement/Dues.java`, `Dues.shown`): a claim's live due is now its figure raised to the floor first, plus the late charge worked out on that floored figure. It used to be figure plus charge, with the floor applied last. Statements, settling, period close, rollups and the open/review thresholds all get their due from this one method, so they all follow. A statement therefore binds the floored figure. Settled dues stay frozen, and corrections (negative amounts) still get no floor and no charge.
- **Front end** (`features/rates/rates.ts`, `claimDue`): the same reorder, so the screen matches the server.
- I updated the doc comments that described the old order in `ClaimStatusChange.java` and `SaveClaimStatus.java`.

**Test results** (`PORT=3187 bin/e2e`)
- **Pass:** "floor before late charge" and "scenario 2".
- **Fail, scenario 1:** at line 231 the spec expects the `sheet-parent` text to be the literal `"__SHEET__-p"`, but the app shows the real id (`<sheetId>-p`). It looks like a placeholder that never got filled in. The due checks before that line passed.
- **Fail, scenario 3:** at line 1030 the spec expects Fay's 20.00 claim dated 2026-02-25 to be added, but the app refuses it. Fay's terms are 3 business days, so the due-by is 2026-03-02, inside period P1 (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-15), which the test closed by hand earlier. The app already refuses a new claim whose due-by falls in a hand-closed period. I didn't loosen that rule because it has nothing to do with this change request. If the spec is right here, that period rule needs its own change.

The first run on the default port 3000 failed every test because the app couldn't start its web server, most likely because the port was busy. Other servers are running on ports 3001–3004 on this machine. If that happens again, set a different `PORT` when running `bin/e2e`.
